cards.title: LS
cards.description_long: The 'ls' command lists files and directories in the current folder. It has multiple options to show hidden files, detailed info, sort output, etc.

main_commands.explanation: List all visible files and directories
Include hidden files starting with '.'
Show detailed info: permissions, owner, size, date
Detailed info with human-readable file sizes
Sort files by modification time, newest first

List files sorted by modification time
Combine flags to list hidden files in long format
Check human-readable sizes of all files

cards.title: CD
cards.description_long: The 'cd' command changes your current working directory. You can navigate using absolute paths or relative paths.

main_commands.explanation: Move to /home/user directory (absolute path)
Go one directory up (parent directory)
Go two levels up from current directory
Switch back to the previous directory
Move to your home directory

cards.title: PWD
cards.description_long: The 'pwd' command prints the full path of the current working directory. It's useful to confirm your location in the filesystem.

main_commands.explanation: Print the absolute path of current directory
Print logical path (follow symlinks)
Print physical path (resolve symlinks)
Show current directory using environment variable
Change directory to /tmp and print current path

activity: Switch to /tmp and verify your location
Use environment variable to print working directory
Combine cd and pwd in a single command

cards.title: MKDIR
cards.description_long: The 'mkdir' command is used to create one or more new directories in the filesystem. You can specify a path or create multiple directories at once. It is a basic and essential command for organizing files and directories. Options like '-p' allow creating nested directories in one command. Beginners should practice creating directories safely in lab environments.

main_commands.explanation: Create a directory named 'new_folder'
Create multiple directories at once
Create nested directories if parent doesn't exist
Create directory in home Documents folder
Verbose output showing directory creation

activity: Create multiple directories in one command
Check directory creation with verbose output

cards.title: RMDIR
cards.description_long: The 'rmdir' command is used to remove empty directories from the filesystem. It only works if the directory contains no files or subdirectories. For non-empty directories, 'rm -r' is used instead. Beginners should be cautious to avoid accidental deletion of important directories. Practicing in lab or sandbox environments is recommended.

main_commands.explanation: Remove an empty directory named 'old_folder'
Remove multiple empty directories at once
Remove non-empty directory recursively
Verbose output showing removed directories
Ignore errors if directory is not empty

activity: Use verbose output to confirm deletion
